name: malbolge
desc: Deliberately difficult to program esoteric programming language
why: A famously hostile esoteric language designed to be nearly impossible to program, a perfect door into strange computing history.

brief.what_it_is: Malbolge is a deliberately difficult esoteric programming language, and this package is the 2004 edition of its release bundle. It contains two interpreters, one in C (malbolge.c) and one in Perl (malbolge.pl), plus several sample Malbolge programs. The README names nop.mal, answer.mal, copy.mal (an implementation of cat), and bb.mal (which outputs an uuencoded gzip of the 99 Bottles of Beer lyrics). The README does not describe the input and output formats in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no motivation beyond noting that Malbolge has been around for a long time and turned out to have some helpful features. It says some useful, if trivial, programs have since been written in it, and this package collects them.
brief.install_notes: The README does not describe how to build or run the interpreters, what runtime the Perl version needs, or any first-run steps. The brew formula exposes a single executable named malbolge.
brief.standout: Malbolge's reputation for being nearly impossible to program is the main draw. This bundle also includes a working cat program (copy.mal) and a program that prints song lyrics, which show the language doing real work. The README itself is a short, dry changelog-style note rather than a manifesto.
brief.status: Quiet. The only dated item is the 2004 edition label. The README has no later release date, version number, or commit history, so I could not confirm current maintenance.
brief.caveats: The README is very thin: it has no usage examples, no build instructions, no license statement, and no links to documentation. The Perl and C interpreters are both bundled, but the README does not say which one the brew executable corresponds to. The description of Malbolge as 'famously hostile' comes from the scout notes, not from this README.
quotes: Quite a long time has passed since Malbolge was released.
It turned out to have quite a few helpful features, and some useful (albeit trivial) programs have emerged.
